mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher when GDP increases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when UNRATE drops below 4% in majority of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment combined with higher federal funds rate indicates economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite the joint condition in most cases.

mechanism_narrative: Lower federal funds rate during easing stimulates investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when FEDFUNDS is below 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates strong supply chains, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positively correlated with industrial production growth.

mechanism_narrative: Increased housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when housing starts exceed 1350 in most cases.

mechanism_narrative: Job gains with decreased retail sales signal economic imbalance, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite the joint condition in most cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment during late-cycle expansion may lead to inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite low unemployment in late-cycle (t-test p > 0.05).
